brief: 8 mistakes I made as a first-time founder that cost me $250K. What I'd do differently — concrete, no generic advice.

slots.title: 1. Salaries, the silent killer
slots.body: I spent $94K on salaries for a product nobody wanted yet. Start with contractors and validate revenue first.

slots.title: 2. Product, the validation gap
slots.body: We spent $40K in dev time on features users never requested. Sell the promise first; build only after pre-orders.

slots.title: 3. Vesting, the legal bomb
slots.body: A co-founder left month four with 40% equity locked up. We paid $30K in legal fees to unwind a handshake deal.

slots.title: 4. Ads, the unit economics lie
slots.body: I poured $58K into Facebook campaigns with a $3 LTV. We never modeled payback period and bled cash instantly.

slots.title: 5. Stack, the engineering vanity
slots.body: We ran Kubernetes and microservices for a hundred-user app. That infrastructure cost $16K in unused tooling and slowed every deployment.

slots.title: 6. Terms, the control trap
slots.body: I accepted a 3x liquidation preference for a small check. It cost $20K in legal review and blocked future raises.
